tldr: One AI drug-discovery round was bigger than most countries' monthly startup funding. Money is flowing, but to fewer, larger bets.
context:
Isomorphic Labs, which applies AI to drug discovery, raised a $5B Series C. On the same day, Genesis AI raised a $500M Series A at a $3.5B post-money valuation to build robots for dexterous industrial work. Nine financings that day added up to more than $6.6B.

A tracker counted 371 announced rounds worth $38.2B in November through the 16th, with a median round of $15M and AI the busiest category.

numbers.k: Genesis AI valuation after a $500M Series A

whyPM:
The gap between the median round and the megarounds is the story: a few AI companies can outspend whole categories on talent, compute and distribution.

If you compete with one of them, pick ground where money doesn't decide: domain data, distribution you already own, or regulated workflows that take time to earn.
bull: Huge rounds fund long research bets (drug discovery, robotics) that smaller cheques can't, and they pull talent and suppliers into new categories.
bear: Concentration raises the bar for everyone else, and this week's AI stock selloff shows how quickly sentiment can turn on capital-heavy bets.
unknowns: Who led the Isomorphic round and at what valuation?
